$comment: Deny rules specific to THIS repository, merged into the generated policy by
scripts/dogfood.mjs. They are here rather than in the product's standing library because
extending that library changes behaviour for every customer, which is not a decision a
run gets to make on its own initiative.
Found 2026-08-16, in the first ten minutes of installing our own product: `npm publish`
was denied by the standing library, but `git tag v0.9.0` was ALLOWED — and on this repo
the tag IS the release. publish.yml fires on `v*`. So the single most repeated rule in
all eleven scheduled job prompts — 'never publish a release, no v* tags' — was enforced
nowhere. It lived in prose, outside the auditable ruleset, believed by everyone.
That is the exact failure this product exists to name, found by pointing it at ourselves.

deny.rule: Never create a release tag. A v* tag publishes to npm and cannot be taken back.
deny.reason: A v* tag triggers publish.yml and reaches strangers irreversibly. Releasing is automatic, via the release gate, or it is Patrik's.
